subject.title: RFC: Readiness Conditions and Standard Hosting Profiles

question: Should OpenClaw adopt canonical readiness conditions, the plugin readiness-provider API, and named standard hosting profiles as stable core contracts?
rationale: The implementation and runtime proof are strong, but only maintainers can commit the project to permanent public API, configuration, upgrade, and hosting-support semantics.

options.title: Accept the complete contract
options.body: Sponsor the unified condition model, provider API, standard profiles, compatibility projections, and staged release-conformance roadmap.

options.title: Accept a narrower first phase
options.body: Adopt normalized core readiness conditions first while deferring plugin providers, operator profiles, or the CLI.

options.title: Decline core hosting profiles
options.body: Retain the fixed Gateway readiness model and leave hosting-posture composition to downstream operators.

recommendation.title: Accept the complete contract
recommendation.body: Sponsor the unified condition model, provider API, standard profiles, compatibility projections, and staged release-conformance roadmap.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the broadest merged history across the Gateway and plugin-extension boundaries and is the strongest available routing candidate for the cross-cutting product contract.
